Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that as marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering crucial questions about its effects on mental health.
  • According to recent reports, published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition.
  • Sources indicate that the findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering crucial questions about its effects on mental health. A major upcoming study suggests that people who struggle to control their cannabis use face a substantially greater likelihood of experiencing suicidal thoughts.

According to recent reports, published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition. Despite major shifts in marijuana laws and public attitudes, this troubling association remained remarkably consistent over a decade.

Sources indicate that the findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. Researchers examined data collected between 2014 and 2023, a period when cannabis became increasingly accessible across the United States.

In a recent development, "What surprised me most was not that cannabis use disorder was associated with suicidal thoughts, but that this association did not appear to strengthen over time," stated lead author Tosin Philip Oyetunji, MPH, a doctoral student in public health at the University of California, Merced. "[Yet,] it remains an key mental health concern that deserves attention.".

Cannabis and Suicidal Thoughts Show a Persistent Link.

Recent findings suggest that the connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thinking was observed across different age groups, sexes, and racial and ethnic backgrounds. However, women and younger adults showed particularly elevated risks.

Importantly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for depression, psychological distress, and other factors that could influence mental health outcomes.

Recent findings suggest that the consistency of the results was especially notable given how dramatically the cannabis landscape has changed. Recreational marijuana is now legal in half of U.S. states, and cannabis products have become increasingly potent. These developments have raised concerns among public health experts about whether broader access might contribute to worsening mental health.

Yet the study offers some reassurance on that particular question. Sidra Goldman-Mellor, PhD, a professor of public health at UC Merced and the study's senior author, noted that the association between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts did not become stronger during the 10 years examined.

"Suicidal ideation does not seem to have increased among people with cannabis use disorder, despite all this legal and social change," explained Goldman-Mellor. Yet, "people with cannabis use disorder are still at a very substantially increased likelihood of experiencing serious suicidal thoughts, and that's not something that is widely understood.".

Why Cannabis Use Disorder Matters.

The researchers stress that these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that everyone who uses marijuana faces the same elevated risk.

The study focused specifically on cannabis use disorder, a condition in which people have difficulty controlling their marijuana consumption even when it causes problems in their lives. Someone with the disorder may continue using cannabis despite harmful consequences or repeated attempts to cut back.

This distinction is vital because problematic cannabis use differs from occasional or otherwise nonproblematic consumption.

The findings also do not establish that cannabis use disorder directly causes suicidal thoughts. Because the research identified an association rather than a cause-and-effect relationship, it cannot determine whether problematic cannabis use contributes to suicidal thinking, whether underlying mental health difficulties contribute to both conditions, or whether other factors help explain the connection.

Nevertheless, the results point to a significant mental health concern that deserves greater recognition, particularly among people seeking help for problematic cannabis use.

Researchers Urge Greater Mental Health Screening.

One practical implication is that health care professionals should look beyond cannabis consumption itself when evaluating patients with cannabis use disorder.

Recent findings suggest that rather than focusing exclusively on depression or substance use symptoms, clinicians may benefit from asking patients directly about suicidal thoughts as part of a broader mental health assessment. This could help identify people who need additional care but whose struggles might otherwise remain unnoticed.

According to recent reports, "Someone seeking help for cannabis use disorder may also be experiencing suicidal thoughts that are not immediately apparent," stated Oyetunji. "The goal is not to assume that everyone with cannabis use disorder is suicidal but to identify those who may need additional assessment, treatment, or support.".

It has been revealed that the study arrives at a time when marijuana is increasingly viewed as a relatively low-risk substance. Public perceptions have shifted considerably, and negative attitudes toward cannabis have declined alongside expanding legalization and social acceptance.

However, these changes have not eliminated the mental health challenges associated with cannabis use disorder. Even though the strength of the association with suicidal thoughts did not increase over the study period, the elevated odds remained substantial.

The researchers suggest that health care providers, policymakers, and community organizations can play an vital role by improving awareness, identifying vulnerable individuals, and making appropriate mental health support more accessible.

As attitudes toward marijuana continue to evolve, the findings serve as a reminder that the needs of people experiencing problematic cannabis use should remain a public health priority.

Stated Oyetunji, "As cannabis becomes more accessible and socially accepted, we should ensure that the people struggling with its use are not overlooked.".

Recent findings suggest that yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Upcoming Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

In a recent development, however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Upcoming Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Industry observers note that furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Industry observers note that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no confirmed platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is finally here. It's been a long 13 year wait for a latest instalment to the Grand Theft Auto series, and regardless of whether this is your first time playing one of these games or if you're a series veteran just in need of a helping hand, our GTA 6 Chapter 1 walkthrough is here to guide you through the first set of missions in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that there's a massive amount of things to do and see in Leonida, so much so that it can be a little overwhelming at times – especially when the game starts throwing missions at you all at once. So we're going to take things slow in our Chapter 1 walkthrough of GTA 6.

It has been revealed that this chapter 1 walkthrough is in-progress, and will lead you from the Prologue and into mission 7, and spotlight some optional activities you can do along the way. We'll be updating this guide over time with new mission breakdowns. I also wanted to flag some GTA 6 essentials before you get too far into the game:.

How the honor system works in Leonida.

How your Relationship Status works.

Don't forget to log your progress.

With that out of the way, the Prologue mission is the first part of the GamesRadar+ GTA 6 Chapter 1 walkthrough. This guide highlights your first steps into Leonida, teaches you the basics of control, and introduces you to Lucia Caminos – one of two playable protagonists in Grand Theft Auto 6.

According to recent reports, you gain control of Lucia at the Leonida Penitentiary, looking through a window out at the prison yard. Your first task is to interact with your cellmates, giving you a feel for the basic controls that will serve you well in the hours to come:.

Sources indicate that once you've spoken with your cellmates, you need to go with the prison guard waiting at the door. He will lead you to area A102 and ask you to wait while he organizes a transfer to a different block. This is a good opportunity for you to perfect your conversational skills, so hold L2 / LT and press X / A to speak with different inmates until the guard calls you over.

Industry observers note that the guard will lead you into Counselor Gates' office for an interview to determine whether Lucia is eligible for early parole through an early release program due to overcrowding. This will initiate a brief flashback which helps set the stage on how Lucia ended up incarcerated, and teach you combat basics.

Once you take control of Lucia in the bank, you'll need to hold L2/LT to aim your concealed handgun. Pointing your weapon at each person in the bank – regardless of whether it's a civilian, employee, or guard – will prompt a different reaction, and you can press Square/X to matter threats.

Industry observers note that aim your gun at the bank teller by holding L2/LT and press Square/X to threaten them and they will begin to empty the cash register. Walk up to the window of the cashier desk and press Triangle / Y to begin picking up individual bundles of cash.

According to recent reports, regardless of how quickly you grab the cash, one civilian will decide to get involved and grab Lucia. You'll need to quickly press Square/X to break their hold. With the security alarm blaring and cops on your tail, you'll quickly pick up the basics of movement:.

Recent findings suggest that use this knowledge to get across the rooftop and down to the street level. Your objective now is to lose the cops, and it's up to you how you approach this task. Sadly, with a two star Wanted level there's only so far you can get, so it won't be long before you're caught by the cops and Busted.

A brief cutscene will now play showing Lucia negotiating with Counselor Gates for early release, with Lucia insisting that she'll be on her best behavior as she reunites with her partner, Jason Duval, for a period of house arrest at his spot in Leonida Keys.

Set in a world of magic and modernity co-existing side-by-side, it features gorgeous anime-inspired art and interesting gameplay. Or at least the latter is what the Astrae Oratio dev team will hope.

With the recent end of their closed beta, the Astrae Oratio game director Jong-Gyu Lim offered us some of their thoughts on the results and, in particular, how well it was received by fans. With combat being so different to other games on the market, Lim has been eager to demonstrate to fans that their feedback has been heard.

Recent findings suggest that "Many people pointed out elements that disrupt the flow and tempo of combat, and the development team also deemed these to need improvement. We are refining things so that combat can be enjoyed more smoothly by the official launch.".

However, Lim was also quick to reiterate exactly why Astrae Oratio's more interactive take on combat, contrary to a popular trend in other games towards auto-battler mechanics, was so vital.

"We wanted to capture both the tactile satisfaction of directly controlling your character and the strategic thrill of planning your next move. The starting point for combat in Astrae Oratio was combining the excitement of fighting games, things like reading your opponent’s movements, finding openings, and stringing together combos, with the resource management of turn-based games.

"What connects these is AP, the action resource. By choosing whether to invest in attacks and press the advantage or save it for responding, you find yourself thinking about both moment-to-moment inputs and your next move.

"Ultimately, we want to bring each character’s unique fighting style to life in combat and allow players to gain the advantage using their own judgment and inputs.".

Notably, although Lim does defend the original design intent behind how Astrae Oratio will work, he also went into detail on the specific pain points from players that they wanted to address.

"The forced use of specific characters, the disappearance of remaining AP when an enemy is defeated, and the insufficient rewards for successful parries that you mentioned are also notable feedback items we identified in that process. The current rules are not set in stone.

Sources indicate that "In particular, we plan to rework how leftover AP is handled so the flow of combat isn’t interrupted, and enhance parrying so that landing a successful parry feels genuinely rewarding. We will continue making adjustments based on the feedback from the test and by validating those results moving forward.".

All of these are, of course, valid concerns for many fans. But it's clear that the folks behind Astrae Oratio have confidence in their vision for combat. And in truth I can't blame them, as nowadays it seems as though combat is considered a 'solved problem', even where there's room to experiment and tweak.

So, in that regard, it's refreshing to see NCSoft's development team look more closely at what they can do to change things. Although if you are concerned about playing all the time manually and the pressure that it invokes, Lim was quick to point out changes which will make it easier for those wanting a more laid-back experience.

In a recent development, "To preserve the advantages of manual combat, where you make your own judgments and inputs, we proposal to maintain a certain degree of efficiency over auto-combat. However, to reduce the fatigue of repeated play, we are improving the pacing of auto-combat and also reviewing additional speed-up options.

"We also plan to significantly expand the limits on boosted play to avoid inconveniencing players, and while it won’t be a traditional sweep mechanic, we are developing a feature that allows you to acquire needed resources more conveniently. We will strive to deliver both the thrill of hands-on combat and the convenience needed for daily grinding.".

Overall, it seems as if the closed beta was a success for Astrae Oratio, and even the developers themselves admit that it was exciting to get new feedback from players out in the wild.

"The positive responses to the story and art gave us great encouragement. We also received diverse opinions on what felt fun in the combat system and what needs improvement, and based on this, we will strive to deliver an even more polished version.".

And as for how it felt for fans to get their hands on Astrae Oratio from all across the world?

It has been revealed that "There were differences in detailed reactions by region, but the way customers appreciated the appealing content we intended to present was similar. It gave the sense that there are no borders when it comes to what you love. Indeed, you could say 'when it comes to otaku, we are the world.'" I think that Astrae Oratio is shaping up to be a particularly interesting new entry in NCSoft's catalogue. And while I can never truly forgive them for canning the surprisingly fun little MOBA called Battle Crush, I think that Astrae Oratio and Limit Zero Breakers make for exciting substitutes.

It has been revealed that if you want to see what they'll be competing against when Astrae Oratio does launch, well, there's no need to trawl through our back catalogue to find out. Instead, why not dig into our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) for some of our choice picks?

#4985. Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment

Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1191 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An international research team has developed a new technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease.
  • Recent findings suggest that the technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain.
  • Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An international research team has developed a new technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease. In experiments involving mice with Parkinson's-like symptoms, the approach significantly improved movement problems without requiring permanently implanted electrodes.

Recent findings suggest that the technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain. When exposed to an external magnetic field, these particles generate tiny forces that activate nearby nerve cells. Unlike conventional brain stimulation treatments, which rely on surgically implanted electrodes, the new approach uses magnetic forces to influence brain activity. The findings, published in Advanced Science, come from researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), RWTH Aachen, and the Universities of Maastricht (the Netherlands) and Leuven (Belgium).

Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.

According to recent reports, parkinson's disease develops as brain cells responsible for producing dopamine gradually break down. Dopamine is a chemical messenger that plays a vital role in controlling movement. As its levels decline, communication within the brain's movement circuits becomes disrupted, contributing to tremors and other motor difficulties.

Sources indicate that for some patients, deep brain stimulation can help control these symptoms. This treatment uses a device known as a brain pacemaker, which is implanted beneath the collarbone and connected to electrodes placed deep inside the brain. The electrodes deliver electrical stimulation to a region called the subthalamic nucleus (STN for short), helping to modify abnormal activity in the brain circuits responsible for movement.

Although this treatment can provide substantial relief, it requires a complex surgical procedure and does not work for everyone.

"The procedure is relatively complex, however, and not always successful," explains Prof. Dr. Danijela Gregurec from the Department of Chemistry and Pharmacy at FAU. "This puts many Parkinson's patients off, and not all patients are suitable candidates for one of these pacemakers.".

The researchers believe magnetic stimulation could eventually provide another option, allowing doctors to influence the same deep brain structures without leaving electrodes permanently implanted.

How Tiny Magnetic Particles Stimulate Brain Cells.

The new technology takes advantage of the ability of certain nerve cells to detect physical pressure and mechanical forces.

It has been revealed that "We use magnetic nanoparticles that we implant in the brain," Gregurec explains. "They have a special shape and a magnetic structure. They were developed in order to transform magnetic fields into tiny mechanical forces.".

Rather than sending electrical pulses directly into the brain, the technique uses these particles to produce extremely small physical movements when a magnetic field is applied.

"The traditional method establishes an electrical connection to the brain," she states. "In contrast, we use the neurons' natural mechanosensors to influence regions deep within the brain.".

The process works by gently changing the shape of nearby nerve cell membranes. Imagine pressing a finger against an inflated balloon and creating a small indentation in its surface. The magnetic particles produce a similar effect on a microscopic scale.

This slight deformation opens specialized channels in the cell membrane that respond to mechanical pressure. Once opened, these channels allow electrically charged particles called ions to enter the nerve cells, changing their electrical activity and providing a way to stimulate the targeted brain circuits.

Magnetic Brain Stimulation Improves Movement in Mice.

In a recent development, to investigate whether the technology could relieve Parkinson's symptoms, the international research team conducted experiments using mice with damage to the same types of dopamine-producing nerve cells affected by the disease in humans. This damage caused movement difficulties resembling those seen in Parkinson's patients.

"Together with our partners from Maastricht, we injected magnetic nanoparticles developed here at FAU into the animals' subthalamic nucleus," Gregurec explains. "That is the very region in the brain that is also an vital target for conventional deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.".

In a recent development, the researchers used precise stereotactic injection techniques to deliver the particles to the intended location. These methods rely on carefully calculated three-dimensional coordinates to guide instruments into specific brain structures. Accurate placement was particularly important because the treatment needed to affect the correct neural circuits involved in movement.

After the particles were positioned, the researchers applied an external magnetic field. The results were encouraging: the mice showed significant improvements in their movement deficits.

"The effect is roughly equivalent to what we would have expected after implanting a brain pacemaker," states Gregurec.

The findings suggest that magnetic nanoparticles could provide a different way to achieve some of the benefits of conventional deep brain stimulation, without the need for permanently implanted electrodes.

Could Future Parkinson's Treatments Use Magnetic Headbands?

Industry observers note that another encouraging finding involved how the brain responded to the implanted particles over time. The magnetic nanoparticles remained in place throughout an observation period lasting several months, and the researchers found no signs of inflammation. This suggests that the particles were well tolerated during the experiments.

Recent findings suggest that however, delivering the particles still required an injection directly into the brain. Gregurec and her colleagues are now investigating ways to make the procedure even less invasive.

Industry observers note that one possibility is to develop particles that could be injected into the bloodstream and then travel into the brain by crossing the blood-brain barrier. This protective boundary normally prevents many substances circulating in the blood from entering brain tissue. Finding a way to deliver the particles across it could eliminate the need for direct brain injections.

The researchers are also exploring compact wearable devices capable of generating the magnetic fields needed for stimulation. One possibility is a headband that patients could put on themselves, potentially making treatment more convenient and adjustable.

These ideas remain at an early stage, and the researchers expect that several more years of development will be needed before the technology could be considered for clinical use.

"Nevertheless, we are convinced that the new method has enormous potential," Gregurec states. "It is not only considerably simpler and cheaper than a conventional brain pacemaker, it is probably also more flexible. Adjusting the parameters of the magnetic field would allow us to control the nanoparticles more accurately.".

Recent findings suggest that beyond its potential medical applications, the technology could also become a valuable scientific tool. By allowing researchers to stimulate nerve cells through carefully controlled mechanical forces, it offers a newly introduced way to explore how physical changes at the cellular level influence brain activity.

Although the treatment has so far been demonstrated only in animals, its ability to improve movement without permanently implanted electrodes represents a promising step toward upcoming approaches to Parkinson's disease and brain stimulation.

Recent findings suggest that nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. #4981. 8 Soulslikes With the Most Unforgiving Checkpoint Systems

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (921 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

8 Soulslikes With the Most Unforgiving Checkpoint Systems

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finding the next checkpoint in any Soulslike game feels like a godsend.
  • While there are Soulslikes out there that are generally pretty generous when it comes to their checkpoint systems, there are others that are extremely punishing.
  • In this list, we take a look at eight games that have a punishing checkpoint system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding the next checkpoint in any Soulslike game feels like a godsend. After fighting through waves of enemies, gathering a ton of loot and experience points, you’re hopeful that the next checkpoint will come soon so you can level up.

While there are Soulslikes out there that are generally pretty generous when it comes to their checkpoint systems, there are others that are extremely punishing. The more punishing checkpoint systems tend to feel more rewarding, but are also the cause of a lot of frustration.

In this list, we take a look at eight games that have a punishing checkpoint system. Whether it's because their checkpoints are too far apart, levels feature too many enemies, or the runbacks to the bosses are miserable, you will find it in this list.

Demon’s Souls essentially started the idea of including unforgiving checkpoint systems in games. Unlike later FromSoftware games that provide plenty of shortcuts and checkpoints near challenging encounters, Demon’s Souls often forces players to replay lengthy sections of a level.

Industry observers note that the Shrine of Storms and Valley of Defilement are two clear examples of this, where the trek between checkpoints, otherwise known as Archstones, is more intimidating than the bosses themselves. Plus, the game’s unique “World Tendency” mechanic, which makes the world more challenging with each death, makes the lack of checkpoints hit even harder.

Lords of the Fallen’s most unique trait is its checkpoint system, which comes in the form of Vestiges. There are permanent Vestiges and Umbral Flowerbeds, temporary Vestiges that players can activate by planting a seed.

While the permanent Vestiges remain at all times, they are extremely far apart in each level, making it so the player has to rely on planting Vestige Seeds into Umbral Flowerbeds. However, this is easier mentioned than done considering Vestige Seeds are generally rare.

Sources indicate that even though Hollow Knight: Silksong is primarily a Metroidvania, and an excellent one at that, it has enough Soulslike elements that make it fit right at home in the genre. And it fits right at home in this list due to its checkpoint system that can be a downright pain in the butt.

Silksong’s checkpoints are rarely near each other. This is especially punishing in a game like Silksong since dying could lead to the player having to repeat a series of platforming challenges. The lack of checkpoints is especially noticeable for some bosses, like The Last Judge and Groal the Great, each with extensive platforming runbacks to the boss arena.

Dark Souls 2’s infamous bonfires aren’t disliked because of their distance from each other, but for the excruciating number of enemies between them. Some gaps between bonfires are littered with too many elite enemies, mobs, traps, and more, making the game sometimes feel like a chore.

The checkpoints are especially punishing when it comes to the game’s bosses, since the bosses are not easy and the runbacks between bonfire and boss arena are excruciatingly long. Having to trek all the way back to the boss arena just to attempt to boss fight again is simply tiring.

Mortal Shell’s checkpoint system is unforgiving for multiple reasons. One, they are generally well-hidden and away from areas worth exploring, and two, Mortal Shell’s level design is filled with interconnecting paths that make it easy to get lost.

Usually in a Soulslike, you lose experience points or resources upon death, such as “Souls” in Dark Souls. However, in Mortal Shell, you lose both Tar and Glimpses, which are two necessary resources for character progression. Losing two notable resources instead of one makes finding a checkpoint even more stress-inducing.

Industry observers note that the checkpoint system in Bleak Faith: Forsaken is punishing due to the absurdly large environments players will be exploring during a playthrough. Not only are the levels huge, but they are also genuinely confusing, causing players to easily get lost.

Industry observers note that due to the low budget and only a three-person team behind the project, it can sometimes feel like you’re playing a game with no clear direction. This, plus the fact that checkpoints are few and far between, can make it feel like you’re always being punished.

Hellpoint’s checkpoints come in the form of Breaches, and even though they are key to progression, they don’t act like your typical Soulslike checkpoint. For starters, they don’t restore your healing supplies, meaning they can’t be used as a way to survive longer. Players have to instead focus on inventory management for that.

On the other hand, Breaches are scattered throughout large levels, meaning there are tons of enemies between them. Dying in Hellpoint results in dropping Axions, an notable resource for leveling, but also spawns a ghost of your past character that you have to fight when returning to the spot of death. This can make reaching the next checkpoint even more difficult than before.

Bloodborne has some notoriously distant checkpoints, especially when compared to other FromSoftware titles and Soulslikes in general. This is punishing enough, but the fact that the game is downright brutal when it comes to the amount of damage enemies deal, distant checkpoints feel even more punishing.

It has been revealed that some examples of a few lamp checkpoints include Nightmare of Mensis and Forbidden Woods, some of the hardest areas in the game that have long stretches of dangerous enemies. Players can expect to die many times in these areas alone before even coming close to the next checkpoint, depending on skill level.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

In a recent development, europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Industry observers note that spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

According to recent reports, china will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

It has been revealed that first Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

According to recent reports, the change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

In a recent development, riot has not yet stated how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

Latest Update: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (717 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control.
  • To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.
  • Studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control. These drugs also influence biological processes involved in brain function, raising questions about whether they could help preserve memory and thinking abilities.

To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.

Studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory. However, research involving humans has produced less consistent findings. Analyses of patient health records have found an association between GLP-1 treatment and a reduced risk of dementia among people with type 2 diabetes. These observational findings are encouraging, but they cannot determine whether the medications themselves are responsible for the lower risk.

More definitive results have also raised questions. In Novo Nordisk's EVOKE and EVOKE+ clinical trials, semaglutide failed to slow the progression of early Alzheimer's disease. Although the treatment affected several biological markers associated with Alzheimer's, those changes did not translate into a measurable slowing of the disease.

Why Weight Loss Drugs May Still Benefit the Brain.

Despite the disappointing Alzheimer's results, researchers believe GLP-1 medications could still offer cognitive benefits to certain groups of patients.

Recent findings suggest that people living with obesity or type 2 diabetes sometimes experience difficulties with attention, planning, and the speed at which they process information. These cognitive problems are often associated with metabolic health and blood vessel function, suggesting they may respond differently to treatment than the changes caused by Alzheimer's disease.

Improving blood sugar regulation, metabolism, or vascular health could potentially help preserve cognitive abilities, even if the same medications cannot slow an established neurodegenerative disease.

Stina Börchers, the review's first author and a researcher affiliated with both the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen, emphasizes the need to determine whether starting treatment earlier could make a difference.

Recent findings suggest that "We need to find out whether these treatments can help people with obesity or diabetes preserve their cognitive abilities, particularly if treatment begins before cognitive problems become established. It is also important to identify which patients might benefit," states Stina Börchers.

Unlocking Upcoming Treatments to Protect Memory.

A central unanswered question is how GLP-1 medications might influence the brain. Their potential cognitive effects could result from improvements in metabolic health, direct actions within the brain, or a combination of both.

Understanding these mechanisms could help researchers identify which patients are most likely to benefit and potentially lead to medications designed specifically to support memory and other thinking abilities.

Christoffer Clemmensen, the review's senior author and a research group leader at the University of Copenhagen, sees an opportunity to use increasingly advanced obesity treatments to explore the connection between metabolism and the brain.

Recent findings suggest that "Obesity medicines are becoming increasingly sophisticated, offering latest opportunities to understand how metabolic regulation influences brain function. By disentangling the direct and indirect effects of these drugs on the brain, we may ultimately be able to develop treatments specifically aimed at preserving cognitive function," notes Christoffer Clemmensen.

In a recent development, the researchers are calling for clinical trials that evaluate memory, attention, and other cognitive abilities beginning when patients first start treatment. Following these changes over time could help establish whether GLP-1 drugs genuinely protect brain function and clarify who might benefit most.

According to recent reports, they also stress that treatment is not without potential drawbacks, particularly for older adults and people who are physically frail. Rapid weight loss can lead to a reduction in muscle mass, which may weaken physical function and offset some of the possible benefits.

Careful monitoring will therefore be essential as researchers investigate whether today's weight loss and diabetes medications could eventually provide latest ways to protect the brain.

Sources indicate that as the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of new content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to enhancement the community on what to expect in 2026.

The quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one update on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s newly introduced blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

It has been revealed that in the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of complications should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

The first stage of the upcoming roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo issues, and other crashes and freezing.

Industry observers note that the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers complications around eating and drinking.

Industry observers note that another important area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more complications join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

In a recent development, the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next upgrade will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported challenges.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally here, but it's digital-only – a reality that GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen likely isn't too keen on, judging by his take regarding publishers' move away from physical games.

According to recent reports, it's no secret that we're gradually moving toward a digital world, with Sony's decision to end physical disc production immediately springing to mind (and GTA 6 coming as a code in a box, of course) – and, it seems, Cohen isn't a massive fan of this move, much like many collectors and gamers themselves aren't. He explains as much in a new interview with Bloomberg, stating that folks should be in control of the media they pay for.

"When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," the chief executive officer argues. It's not only a matter of players being unhappy, either – Cohen claims it's harming brands like GameStop, which rely on physical purchases, trade-ins, and the like. "Unquestionably," he admits, "the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." That does make sense, I suppose.

It has been revealed that he describes how he's been in talks with "the obvious" publishers, detailing why they're not a fan of trade-ins: they lose money. "Of course they don't like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," in Cohen's own words. "They're taking away competition." That checks out, too, I suppose, as I can see why used copies and such could cost companies cash they'd otherwise be receiving themselves.

As for GTA 6 itself, Cohen doesn't explicitly comment on it – but when it comes to presales, it sounds like GameStop has done well enough. "It's a code in a box," he claims, noting that, yes, Grand Theft Auto 6 is exclusively digital. But, "I mean, we're selling a lot of it." Still, I do wonder how different things would look if it were truly physical… although I suppose there wouldn't be much variation at this point.

#4973. This remarkable fresh material could solve a major carbon capture problem

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1126 w)

This remarkable fresh material could solve a major carbon capture problem

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1126 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor.
  • The researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs.
  • Industry observers note that the advance could have notable implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor. Instead of allowing moisture to interfere with the process, the material uses it to help maintain effective carbon capture.

The researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. Their findings, published in Angewandte Chemie, could help make carbon capture more practical and affordable for factories and other industrial facilities.

Industry observers note that the advance could have notable implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Industrial operations, including the burning of fossil fuels to produce energy, are major sources of atmospheric carbon dioxide. In the United States, industry accounts for 30% of total greenhouse gas emissions, according to the Environmental Protection Agency.

A New Material That Overcomes a Major Carbon Capture Problem.

The new material, called BVR-X, has an unusual internal structure that keeps water and carbon dioxide largely separated within its microscopic pores. By directing the two substances into different regions, it prevents water molecules from occupying the spaces needed to capture carbon dioxide.

"This internal organization helps the material work under conditions that more closely resemble real industrial emissions," mentioned Kyriakos Stylianou, professor of chemistry in the OSU College of Science.

MOFs are crystalline materials built from positively charged metal ions connected by organic molecules called ligands, which act as linkers. The metal ions form connection points, or nodes, while the linkers join them together into repeating structures resembling tiny cages. These structures contain extremely small pores that can trap gas molecules on their internal surfaces through a process called adsorption, much like a sponge holds substances within its structure.

One of the advantages of MOFs is their remarkable adaptability. Scientists can combine different metals and organic linkers to create materials with specific characteristics. According to Stylianou, millions of MOF designs are theoretically possible. Researchers have already synthesized more than 100,000 distinct MOFs and predicted the properties of hundreds of thousands more.

Why Carbon Capture Needs Better Materials.

According to recent reports, "The capture of CO2 is critical for meeting net-zero emission targets," said Stylianou, who directs OSU's Materials Discovery Laboratory, known as the MaD Lab. "MOFs have shown a lot of promise because of their porosity and their structural versatility.".

Recent findings suggest that carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas released when fossil fuels are burned. As it accumulates in the atmosphere, it traps heat and contributes to global warming.

One approach to addressing the problem involves removing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Facilities designed for this purpose are beginning to operate in different parts of the world. The world's largest such plant opened in Iceland in 2024, although its annual carbon removal capacity is still relatively small compared with global emissions. According to Stylianou, the facility can capture roughly as much carbon dioxide in one year as about 7,200 cars produce over the same period.

Capturing carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere is another option, and the technologies used for this purpose are considerably more established. At factories and power plants, carbon capture systems can intercept emissions as they travel through exhaust systems and smokestacks. Some of these systems use MOFs to adsorb carbon dioxide molecules from the passing gases.

How Water Makes Industrial Carbon Capture Difficult.

Industry observers note that A major obstacle, however, is that industrial exhaust often contains substantial amounts of water vapor. Many MOFs that perform well in controlled laboratory experiments lose much of their carbon capture ability when exposed to the humid conditions found in actual smokestacks.

The gases can be dried before carbon dioxide is removed, but doing so requires additional equipment and energy. Those costs can become so significant that the overall process is no longer economically practical for industrial use.

BVR-X offers a different approach. Rather than requiring moisture to be removed, the material responds to water in a way that preserves its ability to collect carbon dioxide. Its internal organization allows water and carbon dioxide to occupy different regions, helping prevent the competition that normally undermines carbon capture performance.

According to recent reports, "Water usually makes capturing carbon dioxide more difficult," he said. "Our fresh material does something unusual: It responds to water by changing in a way that lets it keep capturing CO2 effectively even under very humid conditions.".

Strong Performance Under Realistic Industrial Conditions.

Laboratory tests demonstrated that BVR-X could efficiently capture carbon dioxide from a highly humid gas stream containing only 4% carbon dioxide.

That concentration is particularly relevant to emissions from burning natural gas, where carbon dioxide makes up a relatively small proportion of the exhaust. Extracting it becomes especially difficult when large quantities of water vapor are also present.

The experiments therefore tested the material under conditions that resemble an vital real-world challenge, "where separating a small amount of CO2 in the presence of substantial water is particularly challenging," said Stylianou.

Sources indicate that the researchers also found that BVR-X could repeatedly capture and release carbon dioxide without losing its effectiveness over dozens of cycles. This ability to regenerate the material is vital because commercial carbon capture systems must reuse their capture materials many times to keep operating costs manageable.

"And the material can be regenerated and reused, maintaining performance through dozens of capture-and-release cycles and tolerating demanding conditions," he added. "Those are key qualities for practical carbon-capture technologies.".

The results suggest that BVR-X could help overcome a major limitation of existing MOF technologies, particularly in industrial settings where removing moisture from exhaust gases would otherwise be costly.

The study brought together researchers from several institutions. Stylianou worked with MaD Lab members Ankit Yadav, Emmanuel Musa and Andrzej Gładysiak, along with Micah Hickethier, Chun-Wai Chang and Kai Shen Choong from the Oregon State College of Engineering.

Additional collaborators included scientists from the University of California, Berkeley; the University of Oregon; and the ARAMCO Research and Development Center.

Funding was provided by Saudi Aramco, the Murdock Charitable Trust, and a donor-advised fund established by Oregon State University alumni and retired public school teachers Brian and Marilyn Kleiner through the OSU Foundation.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
  • According to recent reports, hoYoverse declared last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
  • The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

According to recent reports, hoYoverse declared last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's enhancement.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that prior to the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 today, Rockstar had been doing its utmost to play just about every aspect of the game’s production outside of explicitly-revealed details as close to the vest as possible.
  • One of those details, and arguably one of the most crucial to the production, is the game’s cast of voice actors.
  • Now that the game is out, the full cast list has been revealed via the in-game credits, which you technically don’t even need to finish the game to see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that prior to the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 today, Rockstar had been doing its utmost to play just about every aspect of the game’s production outside of explicitly-revealed details as close to the vest as possible. That’s the whole reason why that little saga of GTA 6 leaks was such a major deal, because so much about the game was in a proverbial black box before launch. Now, though, the game is finally in the world’s collective hands, and that means every little itty-bitty detail is readily-available for everyone to obsessively comb through.

One of those details, and arguably one of the most crucial to the production, is the game’s cast of voice actors. Ahead of the game’s release, the vast majority of the cast was shrouded in mystery, with the single exception being veteran actor Stephen Root revealing his role as Brian Heder, though naturally, that didn’t stop the rampant speculation from the precious few soundbites we got in the trailers.

Now that the game is out, the full cast list has been revealed via the in-game credits, which you technically don’t even need to finish the game to see. Perhaps unsurprisingly for such a high-profile production, many of the game’s voice actors come from TV and film backgrounds, a testament to Rockstar’s star power magnetism.

In a recent development, first and foremost, let’s get into our two lead characters, and the most important roles in GTA 6, Jason and Lucia, the duo that had successfully captured hearts and minds before the game was even out. Jason is voiced by Dylan Rourke, a television actor who has had a small spattering of roles since 2013, with some standouts including Modern Family, Grey’s Anatomy, Station 19, and In the Vault.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Lucia, the series's first female protagonist, is voiced by Manni L. Perez, who has previously provided incidental roles in GTA 5 and GTA Online. Outside of games, she’s had a lot of experience in various crime demonstrates, such as The Blacklist, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.

Jason is voiced by Dylan Rourke [...] Lucia, meanwhile, is voiced by Manni L. Perez.

According to recent reports, surprisingly, one of the biggest names in the cast aside from the aforementioned Stephen Root is Bobby Moynihan in the role of Jason’s bumbling buddy Cal. Moynihan is a seasoned actor who got his start all the way back in 1996 with roles in live-action and animated film and television like Portlandia, Aqua Teen Hunger Force, and We Bare Bears, though his most decorated gig was various roles on Saturday Night Live since 2008, most notably his recurring character on the “Weekend Update” sketches.

Recent findings suggest that some other names dropped in the credits include Dre'Quan as Naiqui Macabroad, Orlagh Cassidy as Lori Heder, Brad Carter as Donnie, Mallory Wu as Andy, and rappers Hood Brat and Krissy Celess as Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, respectively. You can check out the credits yourself either by beating the game or just checking the in-game settings menu.

If I were a betting man, I’d put money down on most, if not all of the biggest names in this cast making appearances at The Game Awards next month. In fact, Manni L. Perez has already been nominated for Best Performance as Lucia, among the many, many other categories that GTA 6 has been nominated for alongside Game of the Year.

Sources indicate that it’s gonna be a star-studded event, as it often is, of course, but by appearing in the biggest game of the release, quite possibly the entire decade, just about everyone in the GTA 6 cast have just earned some major street cred in the entertainment industry. Obviously, Stephen Root and Bobby Moynihan were already well-established actors, but hopefully, we’ll be seeing a lot more of Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez both in and out of the gaming scene going forward.

You leave a mark like that on entertainment history, and people will start actively seeking you out in every other production you appear in. Hey, maybe they’ll make cameos if we ever get a GTA movie.

#4970. Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1104 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity.
  • The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma.
  • According to recent reports, the study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity. Their findings suggest that certain immune cells found in body fat can help protect against inflammation and metabolic problems, while others may make these harmful effects worse.

The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma. In experiments with mice, researchers found that these cells behave differently depending on biological sex, potentially helping explain why obesity does not affect males and females in the same way.

According to recent reports, the study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik. Their findings challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar cells with relatively few specialized functions. The results also point toward potential newly introduced approaches for treating obesity and its complications.

Six Types of Immune Cells Found in Body Fat.

In a recent development, to investigate the role of eosinophils in obesity, the researchers used high-resolution single-cell sequencing, a technique that allows scientists to examine gene activity in individual cells. They identified six distinct eosinophil populations in adipose (fat) tissue, each with its own pattern of gene expression and potentially different biological functions.

This unexpected diversity suggests that eosinophils play a much more complicated role in metabolic health than previously recognized.

In a recent development, "Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought," said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences in the UCR School of Medicine. "Some populations can protect against obesity, and if we can identify and activate the pathways that produce these protective cells, we may find newly introduced ways to improve metabolic health.".

Why Male and Female Fat Tissue Respond Differently.

One of the most striking discoveries was a difference in the immune cells found in male and female mice.

Female mice possessed a protective population of eosinophils that appeared to communicate more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells present in fat tissue. According to Nair, this cooperation may help create a healthier environment within fat tissue and support better metabolic function.

Recent findings suggest that male mice showed a different pattern. When given a diet high in fat, they were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation. Their fat tissue also contained eosinophils with gene activity patterns suggesting weaker protective functions.

These findings indicate that the effects of eosinophils on obesity depend on more than simply how many of these cells are present. The particular type of eosinophil and its interactions with neighboring immune cells may be equally important.

Sources indicate that "This means the relationship between eosinophils and obesity is not simply a matter of how many eosinophils are present," said Rebecca E. Ruggiero-Ruff, a postdoctoral researcher in Nair's lab and co-first author of the paper. "Their functional characteristics and how they communicate with other immune cells are also critical.".

A Protein That May Help Protect Against Inflammation.

The researchers also identified a protein called RELM alpha that appears to play an notable role in maintaining the beneficial relationship between eosinophils and macrophages.

Produced by macrophages, RELM alpha seemed to help stabilize communication between the two immune cell types in female mice. This interaction may be one reason certain eosinophil populations are better able to support healthy fat tissue.

The finding builds on earlier experiments by the same research group, which revealed that administering RELM alpha to mice produced protective effects. Together, the results suggest that the protein may help regulate immune activity within fat tissue and influence how the body responds to obesity.

Could the Discovery Lead to Better Obesity Treatments?

Recent findings suggest that although the results offer new insight into the biology of obesity, the experiments were conducted in mice. Researchers have also detected eosinophils in fat tissue from people with obesity, but scientists do not yet fully understand what these cells do in the human body.

Nair cautioned that additional research will be necessary before the discovery can be used to develop treatments. One particularly important question is whether therapies targeting the immune system would work differently in men and women.

It has been revealed that "A drug may not activate the same pathways or produce the same effects in males and females, particularly when it targets the immune system," said co-first author Xinru Qiu, a postdoctoral researcher in Godzik's lab. "We need to investigate sex-specific biology more thoroughly so that treatments can be optimized for different patients.".

Understanding these differences could eventually help researchers design more personalized treatments for obesity and the metabolic complications associated with it.

Scientists Initiative to Recreate Human Fat Tissue in the Lab.

The research team is now investigating whether the protective behavior observed in mouse eosinophils can also be studied in human laboratory models.

To accomplish this, the scientists are developing three-dimensional adipose organoids. These miniature laboratory models reproduce certain features of real fat tissue, allowing researchers to examine how eosinophils interact with fat cells and other components of their environment.

The goal is to determine whether changing communication between immune cells could encourage healthier responses in human fat tissue.

"We ultimately hope to develop human adipose organoids that will allow us to investigate whether manipulating immune-cell communication can promote healthier tissue responses," mentioned Godzik, a professor of biomedical sciences and the Bruce D. and Nancy B. Varner Presidential Endowed Chair in Cancer Research.

According to recent reports, the findings raise the possibility that targeting specific immune cell populations, rather than treating all eosinophils as functionally identical, could eventually provide new ways to address obesity and its complications. Whether the same protective mechanisms operate in humans remains an important question for future research.

The research team also included Lauren Vance, Yuxin He, and Djurdjica Coss, who worked alongside Nair, Godzik, Ruggiero-Ruff, and Qiu.

Funding for the study came from the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine, and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine.

The research paper is titled "Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, EDward Gaming have lost captain nobody and CHICHOO, two days after releasing Smoggy to Bilibili Gaming. The VCT China partner team must now rebuild before the China Kickoff in Hangzhou in January.

EDward Gaming have parted ways with CHICHOO and captain nobody, two pillars of the side that won VALORANT Champions 2024. Both players left the VCT China partner team on the same day. EDG declared both exits on Weibo. Their exits end a five-year spell at the organisation.

The departures follow quickly on from Smoggy’s move to Bilibili Gaming. Within a week, three players had gone from the EDG roster. No replacements have been named.

Wang ‘nobody’ Senxu joined EDG on 7 September 2021. He served as the team’s captain and in-game leader. He had started out as the side’s Initiator before taking on those leadership duties. CHICHOO, whose full name is Wan Shunzhi, played the Controller role. Alongside CHICHOO, he formed the core of the only Chinese team to win Champions. That title, sealed on 25 August 2024, made EDG the first organisation from China, and from Asia, to lift the trophy. The team’s total winnings stand at roughly $1,592,287.

Industry observers note that the pair were still central to the side in 2026. At Masters London, CHICHOO and nobody each played 12 maps. Their average combat scores were 179 and 184 respectively. EDG finished third in London and earned $125,000. Their run ended with a 0-3 defeat to Leviatán in the lower bracket final on 20 June 2026.

Where nobody goes next is not yet confirmed. Sheep Esports reported, citing sources, that he is expected to join Trace Esports for 2027. Trace’s Kai and deLb are mentioned to be under contract until the end of 2027. If that move happens, nobody and Smoggy would both start the fresh season with different organisations.

Industry observers note that the timing is awkward for EDG. The organisation was named a VCT partner team on 21 October, on a two-year contract. That deal now begins with a heavily changed roster.

According to recent reports, the China Kickoff is an S-Tier LAN event. It is organised by TJ Sports, Hero Esports and Riot Games. The league’s partner sides make up eight places in the field, with the remaining four split evenly between visiting teams and open qualifier entrants. EDG will need a settled line-up in place to compete there.
