💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck.
  • The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide.
  • By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

Industry observers note that there's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that newly introduced games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

According to recent reports, as for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is right now only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Well folks, it's official: Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are out, and it's presently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (N64) as the highest-rated game ever on Metacritic.

There may yet be time for things to change as more reviews trickle in, but at the time of writing, GTA 6 is sitting at a remarkable 99 on the aggregate website, based on a total of 134 reviews.

Ocarina of Time, meanwhile, has a mere 22 critic reviews making up that lofty 99 average (it was a different time, man), so one could argue that GTA 6's result is probably more impressive – especially in an age in which it's getting harder and harder to make such an impact.

Our pals over at Push Square were emphatic in their praise, calling GTA 6 "the greatest open world game" in their 10/10 review. Meanwhile, our other pals over at Pure Xbox also gave it 10/10, stating "Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come".

It has been revealed that there are 10s all over the damn place, with the only outliers awarding it 9s or 90s at the lowest. It's pretty unprecedented stuff.

We'll keep an eye on things and update this article if GTA 6 does happen to slip below Ocarina of Time. Elsewhere, the latter's Switch 2 remake also released to almost universal acclaim earlier this month. Critic reviews on Metacritic average out at 96, while it also boasts the highest user review score of all time at 9.6.

It has been revealed that what do you make of GTA 6's Metacritic score at the moment? Are you excited to play it for yourself? Let us know with a comment down below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 keeps the actual mandatory crimes very grounded during its opening hours, far from the previous series openings of massive police shootouts and gang wars bursting at the seams. One of the very first jobs Jason is tasked with sounds fairly simple, but is shockingly involved.

To secure some product left behind by an arrested junkie, Brian tasks Jason with securing a red Phoenix, a sleazy sports car with too much weed in the trunk to just walk away with. Getting it out of the police impound is easier said than done, so let’s go over it step by step.

Before you can yoink the car, you’ll need to start its mission, ‘Unwanted Attention’, by meeting with Cal at one of his fishing spots in Corsair Key. Mark his location via your text messages and drive to the northeast down the highway. These roads are tight, so be careful when trying to pull past other drivers.

Recent findings suggest that once you’ve snagged Cal, he’ll explain the job, marking the police impound where the Phoenix is currently being held. Once you arrive, you can choose between charging straight in with your newly acquired gear, or sneaking around the side through a hole in the barbed wire fence surrounding the other walls.

Stealthing through the impound is much simpler, with very few guards on patrol. If you’re looking to keep your Criminal Profile at a Professional level, hug the left side of the impound’s outer wall until you see an opening in the barbed wire, giving you an opportunity to hop in.

Now that you’re inside the impound itself, you’ll need to sneak past the two patrolling guards. One is wandering around the gate itself, while the other is deeper inside, near the red Phoenix. You’ll be prompted to use the Waink It app to help you identify the ride, but it always spawns in the northeast end of the impound, still hooked up to a winch.

The guards’ patrol patterns don’t overlap, so feel free to wander past or choke them out at your own discretion. Remember, nonlethal takedowns are easy ways to pivot your Criminal Profile towards Professional, or you can finish them off if you’re feeling a bit crueler.

In a recent development, once you find the red Phoenix, don’t hop in immediately. Instead, enter the building behind it to find the guard manning the gate itself. Silently take him down, then hit a button on the wall to open the gate. Once the gate is open, lower the winch the Phoenix is attached to and hotwire it.

Now it’s time to bail! Drive straight through the open gate, and you’ll become Wanted, but since all the local cops are either unconscious or checking on their unresponsive allies, you’ve got a window before they arrive. Stick to backstreets or off-road routes to lose the cops quick.

Recent findings suggest that once you’re all clear, head back over to Hamlet and visit the marked Spray N’ Pray shop to change the car’s paint job. Any will do the trick, even if losing the Phoenix decal is a shame. Once you do, you’ll be able to drop it off at Brian’s Garage for your reward, just enough to buy a latest outfit to get off the radar completely.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major enhancement arrives March 24, adding two fresh Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

It has been revealed that among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A substantial challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier promptly.

Our first fresh arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Industry observers note that being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

According to recent reports, outside of all the very vital action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have declared that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find fresh jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

Recent findings suggest that this news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's no shortage of limited and unique Magic: The Gathering cards in the world, from old cards with limited copies left in the wild to newer serialized cards, but what makes the card we're talking about today so cool is that it may be the very first card of its kind, and it has a fun story behind it.

In a recent development, I spend a lot of time looking for cool and interesting Magic stories around the world, but this one found me! A Magic player named Mike Austin reached out about what is currently the only copy of the foil borderless Bruce Banner / The Incredible Hulk card (#0359), signed by actor Lou Ferrigno and graded by CGC. As someone who loved the look of the Incredible Hulk card when it was previewed, especially due to its ability to go infinite when paired with a card like Caltrops and something to give it invincibility, I wanted to know more about how this card came to be. So, here's the story of how Lou Ferrigno ended up signing his first Magic: The Gathering card.

It has been revealed that the story of this awesome card starts with owner Mike finding a copy of Bruce Banner / The Incredible Hulk inside a Marvel Super Heroes Pack. It's the borderless foil variant with the green background, and while the comic covers are considered the most valuable cards in the set, this one is just as cool because the artwork pops off the vibrant green background.

According to recent reports, mike then took this card to GalaxyCon with the goal in mind of having the original Hulk actor, Lou Ferrigno, sign it. Luckily for Mike, he achieved this goal and even did so with a CGC witness to verify the signature in person. On top of that, during a polite back-and-forth with the actor, Mike says Ferrigno claimed, "I've never signed another Magic: The Gathering Incredible Hulk card before today.".

Recent findings suggest that this was an absolute dream for Mike, and not necessarily because of the value it adds to the card; of course, there is always the reality where Ferrigno simply didn't know he was signing a Hulk Magic card previously, and it could be that this was just the first time he was seeing one of the borderless foils, which are very eye-catching. On the flip side, given that the Marvel MTG set had been released just a few weeks before this encounter, it's highly likely this was the first MTG card he signed; sadly, that is virtually impossible to prove. Regardless, it's a great story to carry around with the card and share with friends and enthusiasts alike.

You can read a more detailed timeline of events over on MTGCommand where Mike has documented the journey of having the card signed and graded.

It has been revealed that after submitting the card for grading, Mike waited just over two months for it to be returned, and when it was, the card itself received a CGC grade of 8, which he admits he was a little disappointed by. The good news, however, is that the autograph grade came back as a 10, more than making up for the lost points on the card itself.

There are at the moment only five CGC-graded versions of this card; the other four have higher grades than Mike's, but none are signed by Lou Ferrigno, and from a quick look across other grading services and online listings, we can find no other Lou Ferrigno-signed Hulk MTG cards. We'd be fairly confident in saying that, right now, this is a one-of-a-kind Magic card, not just because it's signed by Ferrigno, but also because it's graded, with the signature verified and authenticated.

Since the Marvel Universes Beyond set launched, more time has passed for people to potentially get their cards signed by Ferrigno, but as of right now, none of those cards are in the public domain as sales listings or gradings.

If you have a Magic card that you feel is just as unique as the one Mike reached out to us with, feel free to do the same!

According to recent reports, on mobile, point-and-click adventures feel right at home. Instead of clicking with a mouse, you can tap objects, and it often feels very intuitive. As such, they're a favourite among our App Army readers. So, whenever one comes along, we like to get their thoughts. This week, we've given them the spooky Cult Vacui. Here's what they said:.

I love the atmosphere you have 24 mins to complete a ritual before you. Get possessed by a demon. The atmosphere is very good, and the artwork is great. My only problem is I have fat fingers. So selection can be difficult. The idea is that certain actions can take up your time. A bit like Blue Prince, I think.

In a recent development, you repeat until you work out the sequence of events. To be honest, I’m not so good at point-and-clicks, but the story and atmosphere keep me hooked. Just the touch controls feel fiddly. The artwork is a nice pixel style. Very much like the classic Lucas art games.

Recent findings suggest that I’m not usually good at point-and-clicks, so what really grabbed me here is the unique time-management mechanic. Every action ticks down the clock, creating tension without real-time panic. I definitely struggled at first and died a few times trying to get it right,.

Thankfully, the manual save system (allowing you multiple save points) helped me go back and try different strategies. Combined with the eerie graphics and creepy atmosphere, it was much more enjoyment than frustration. It's a short (about two hours) atmospheric winner on iOS.

Cult Vacui is an old-school point-and-click adventure where you play as a man possessed by a demon and must find a way to exorcise the demon. In the first part of the game, you have a limited number of moves to get rid of the demon. This involves finding and manipulating objects to perform an exorcism ritual.

Recent findings suggest that the graphics are atmospheric and pixelated and look like a PC game from the 90s. There is no hint function, and the tight number of moves can make the first part of the game frustrating. Saying that I enjoyed playing this adventure. I recommend it.

Sources indicate that cult Vacui is a pixel art stylised point-and-click survival horror game. Right from the start, I was pulled into CV’s handcrafted 19th-century setting. Puzzles can be difficult with no hand-holding, and every action takes time away from your 25-minute countdown, adding a real sort of tension to your playthrough.

The whole retro vibe works great too; the minimalistic colour tones of the graphics, along with its eerie soundtrack, create just the right amount of spookiness. Cult Vacui fits perfectly on mobile and deserves a spot on your device. What is the App Army? The App Army is Pocket Gamer's lovely community of mobile game experts. If you're hearing a familiar voice between the '80s hits on GTA 6's Vice City FM, you're not imagining things. 'Weird Al' Yankovic is one of the station's hosts. And Rockstar didn't just bring him in to introduce songs. He's also written some of the game's commercials and voiced the ads for Burger Shot.

In a recent development, yankovic confirmed the news in a Bluesky post on November 19, saying he's playing DJ Al on the game's 'non-stop '80s' station. PC Gamer reports that he shares hosting duties with actress and model Brigitte Nielsen, with both appearing in Rockstar's credits.

In a recent development, the radio gig would be enough to get my attention on its own, but Yankovic also noted he wrote some in-game commercials and provided the voice for Burger Shot's advertisements. If you've spent any time listening to GTA radio, you'll know how much Rockstar enjoys making fun of advertising, so that feels like a particularly good use of him.

Industry observers note that I'm a Weird Al fan (who isn't?), and I'm both surprised and not particularly surprised to see him here. He's the sort of person who can turn a ridiculous idea into something genuinely funny, whether he's parodying a hit song or doing a completely original bit. He's ridiculously talented, and getting him to write fake ads for a GTA game just makes sense.

There's also the fact that Yankovic is a longtime GTA fan himself. He sounded pretty happy about the appearance in his announcement and ended his post by saying he was getting back to playing the game. Hard to imagine a better fit for somebody with his sense of humor.

Sources indicate that as I covered when Rockstar revealed The Chamber 106.6, GTA 6 also has a dedicated metal station hosted by Slayer's Tom Araya and Kerry King. Its preview featured Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer. If anyone could convince two Slayer members and Weird Al Yankovic to host radio stations in the same game, it was probably going to be Rockstar.

Sources indicate that that alone tells you how varied the lineup is. Vice City FM is built around '80s music, while The Chamber gives metal fans somewhere to go. There are country, hip-hop, dance, and plenty of other stations for people who'd rather listen to something else.

If anyone could convince two Slayer members and Weird Al Yankovic to host radio stations in the same game, it was probably going to be Rockstar.

Personally, I'm much more interested in the older music, metal, punk, rock, and alternative side of things than whatever's dominating the pop charts right now. I knew Rockstar would have a wide selection, but the radio-station announcements have pretty much exceeded my expectations. And now they've added Weird Al to the mix.

Recent findings suggest that the commercials are worth paying attention to, too. GTA's radio stations have never been just playlists. The fake products, strange callers, obnoxious hosts, and commercials that sound almost believable are a substantial part of what makes driving around these cities entertaining.

Some of the older games also had excellent celebrity DJs. Axl Rose hosted K-DST in San Andreas, while Max Cavalera took over Liberty City Hardcore in The Lost and Damned. Weird Al feels like another name that belongs on that list, especially with Rockstar letting him write some of the material he'll be performing.

In a recent development, I'm curious to hear what his Burger Shot ads sound like. The fast-food chain is already one of GTA's running jokes, and giving those commercials to someone who has spent decades making audiences laugh at pop culture seems like a pretty safe bet.

Lazlow's departure had a lot of us longtime GTA fans worried about the future of the radio stations, but with Rockstar bringing in people like Slayer's Tom Araya and Weird Al, I'd say they've got that side of things covered.

In a recent development, I would've been happy just knowing there's an '80s station to spend a few hours with while driving around Leonida. Having Weird Al on the microphone, along with the return of a proper metal station, has made exploring GTA 6's radio stations one of my favorite things to do in the game.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies.".

In a recent development, if it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting vital leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers.".

Recent findings suggest that their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote.".

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

So, first things first: As the word "unreleased" amidst that slurry of words from the Steam page suggests, this is not actually a remake of a popular game from the days of yore, although it certainly has the vibe, and actually looks pretty decent as these things go. According to recent reports, what really brings us here, though, is that dogged pursuit of GTA 6. It's obviously coattails marketing, but as PC Gamer's Shaun Prescott noted in 2025, it's a pretty good bit—and Devolver is really sticking with it.

According to recent reports, dead by Daylight has an absolutely massive roster if iconic killers and survivors from horror media that just keeps getting bigger each year, which is getting more ambitious ahead of its gameplay overhaul. Having already shattered its player count this year with the release of Jason, DBD is seemingly teasing yet another collaboration that could bring in heaps of fresh players, especially overseas.

Taking things overseas again after the Nier Automata collaboration event, DBD's developers just posted a teaser advertising the upcoming Hartshorne Mall map release on the 24th of November, which offers an unmistakable reference to none other than Toho's Godzilla.

Although the trailer posted to Dead by Daylight's X account doesn't explicitly confirm that Godzilla is being added as a fresh killer or as themed cosmetics, the trailer highlights Dwight's childhood of stealing a familiar-looking Kaiju toy, before being haunted by a sound that fans instantly recognized as an edited version of Godzilla's iconic roar.

While some fans have speculated that it could have been added for fun or to throw off players, Dead by Daylight is well known for its vague teasers before announcing official collaborations, which has already spawned countless memes about facing off against a building-sized killer camping generators.

More likely being added in the form of a fresh line of in-game cosmetics, some fans like Winter__s have also analyzed the audio to note that the two roars included in the clip include one from the Millennium era of Godzilla, and another used in all three Shin Godzilla, Godzilla: Minus One, and Godzilla (1954) films, possibly hinting towards which adaptations will make it into the game.

Even though it's hard to imagine Godzilla fitting in as a killer, other players have proposed the idea of the collaboration possibly adapting the internet analogue horror series The Man in the Suit, which follows the story of an enraged Godzilla actor who merges with his suit and terrorizes others.

While a body-horror-inspired take on Godzilla would certainly be an interesting way to adapt the legendary monster into the world of Dead by Daylight, the most likely opportunity would likely come from more humanoid skins that pay homage to iconic eras from the titular series, or possibly even thin bodysuits for a few killers, similar to the previous Attack on Titan collaboration.

Alan gets stronger by eating his own cooking.

Recent findings suggest that in an RPG, you’d expect to become stronger by hitting things, but in Kemco’s latest, you do it by eating your own cooking (abs are made in the kitchen, as the saying goes). Leingham Tavern Story: Alan and the Time Goddess is out now on the App Store and Google Play. It’s a dungeon crawler and a restaurant sim at the same time, and there’s an orphanage to save on top.

Recent findings suggest that that orphanage is the whole reason you’re doing any of this. It’s about to close down, and Alan and his mates reckon a busy tavern will make enough money to keep it going. Which means heading down into dungeons for ingredients.

Industry observers note that you can go back to these every day, picking things up from gathering points and getting into turn-based fights with whatever monsters are lurking about. You’ll want better gear for the fights and you’ll want levels too, but like I mentioned, you get most of those from eating when you’re back.

Sources indicate that back at the tavern, you can buy recipes, and you can also mix ingredients yourself and see what you get. There are more than 800 dishes to find. There’s a field out the back for growing vegetables too, plus a fishing spot for when you fancy a break (apparently you can catch something you weren’t expecting, though I’ve no idea what).

In a recent development, then there’s running the place, which is what actually keeps the orphanage going. Once a few dishes are on the menu, you open the doors, and from there it’s a case of changing what you cook to suit the season and whatever customers are into at the time, and working out which of your staff should be doing what. Leingham Tavern Story only comes in English and Japanese, and there’s no controller support either.

Leingham Tavern Story: Alan and the Time Goddess is out now on the App Store and Google Play for $9.99.

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds.".

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director says it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

According to recent reports, A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just swiftly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

  • It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert rolled out on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially rolled out, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert rolled out on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it released. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or proposal to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#4865. Latest Update: Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1572 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game.
  • We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.
  • Sources indicate that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that after dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

Sources indicate that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the strategy or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for upcoming ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”.

According to recent reports, the player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”.

In a recent development, it feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Recent findings suggest that luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

One example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”.

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from major crime stories or not?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”.

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

Sources indicate that rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

In a recent development, there’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”.

In its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

In a recent development, when we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we stated we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, showed that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”.

In a recent development, the game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”.

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It is finally time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5 as we open the doors for Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Now that we are turning to the next chapter, we have to look back on GTA 5 with a fond smile and tearful eyes.
  • GTA 5 had a massive impact on the world, and it is now time to reflect on the game before booting up GTA 6 and moving on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is finally time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5 as we open the doors for Grand Theft Auto 6. This doesn’t mean that we didn’t have some good times with GTA 5, but all good things must eventually come to an end.

Now that we are turning to the next chapter, we have to look back on GTA 5 with a fond smile and tearful eyes. Some of the best memories for people were made with that game. Communities came together, lawsuits were filed, and more.

GTA 5 had a massive impact on the world, and it is now time to reflect on the game before booting up GTA 6 and moving on.

There are multiple memes that were spawned thanks to GTA 5. For instance, Trevor kidnapping a guy’s wife will always live rent free in my head, but one of the biggest was the “Davey, how you doing,” meme.

Sources indicate that the scene is simple; Michael just meets up with Davey at the observatory. Well, this sparked a massive collection of memes, and it was mostly thanks to the ability to initiate the cutscene in different ways.

People started reenacting the cutscene in real life, and doing absurd things in game like crashing a blimp into the observatory to initiate the cutscene. It will forever remain in people’s minds.

While yes, GTA 6 is now here, that doesn’t mean that GTA 5 is gone. While people may be leaving the story behind, the online mode still exists, and it is still one of the most popular online games that exist.

It is estimated that there are around 8.5 to 10 million active consumers in GTA Online each week, and they aren’t going to just abandon the online because of GTA 6, at least not while there isn’t a latest GTA Online to flock to.

It has been revealed that GTA 5 will continue to live on through the online mode for the next year until the next iteration of GTA Online is released. At that point, I may have to write another article.

Grand Theft Auto 5 is the first and only game in the GTA series to have three protagonists: Michael, Trevor, and Franklin. Many people were concerned about there being three protagonists because it might dilute each character.

It has been revealed that to everyone’s surprise, it didn’t dilute any of the characters, and it instead enhanced them. The characters work off each other, and it helped build the narrative.

Industry observers note that despite it being 13 years, there are people who still remember quotes from the game. People can describe full scenes and story beats. It is pretty amazing. That type of dedication never goes away. It’s similar to the adults who can still quote early episodes of SpongeBob.

According to recent reports, can we take a moment to reflect on how many copies of GTA 5 were sold worldwide? The game sold approximately 235 million copies within the last 13 years. This is one of the most sold games in the history of gaming.

According to recent reports, that type of legacy doesn’t just go away. Only a few games have sold more copies than GTA 5, and they include Minecraft and Tetris. That is a very impressive feat.

Recent findings suggest that up until this year, kids have begged their parents to purchase them GTA 5, and adults have caved in to see what the hype was all about. With it being as significant as it was, GTA 5 will never be forgotten. It will go down in gaming history and that is a fact.

Industry observers note that GTA 5 isn’t going to be forgotten anytime soon, and if you want proof, look at the current sales. I don’t mean the sales numbers over the last 13 years, I mean the sales numbers from the last week or so.

Within the last quarter, it is estimated that Rockstar sold another 5 million copies of GTA 5. That is ridiculous when you consider that the game is 13 years old.

The hype around GTA 6 has been increasing sales for past GTA titles, but it has mostly had the effect of increasing the sales number of GTA 5, which means that people will still be playing the story for the next year while they wait for GTA Online 2.0 to be released.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 5 was released during a time when people still got together to play games. While the main focus is connecting with people online, there are many who got together during the time of GTA 5 and played the game together in the same room.

Parties were formed, and people played the game together. They formed a bond, and that bond carried over into GTA Online, where people continued to play together and make memories.

These memories are still with those who played the game together and continue to enjoy the online. I played online with multiple friends and I will forever remember those times we shared before the next evolution of the online is released.

According to recent reports, the Grand Theft Auto series is record-breaking, and there is no doubt about that. GTA 5 alone broke multiple records, and that is something that people won’t forget.

As far as records go, GTA 5 broke the record for highest-24 hour entertainment revenue, best-selling video game in 24 hours, best-selling action-adventure game in 24 hours, highest grossing video game in 24 hours, fastest game to reach $1billion in revenue, and more.

When the game launched, it was a huge deal, and it demonstrates through the number of copies that were sold, and it shows even more through the number of records that were broken by it. In total, it broke at least eight records. I can’t think of another game that has done that, and now it is GTA 6’s turn.

According to recent reports, whenever a massive game comes out that parodies stuff in real life, it is bound to attract a few lawsuits, and boy was GTA 5 the center of quite a few lawsuits over the years. One of the earlier ones was from Daz Dillinger who issued a cease and desist letter.

After that, other celebrities like Lindsay Lohan and Karen Gravano filed lawsuits against Rockstar over GTA 5, with one being over an alleged likeness and the other being about a character who mirrored their life.

There was even once a lawsuit over GTA Online because it didn’t launch with the release of the game and was instead released some time later. While it isn’t the best look, this attention still attracts people to the game and it makes people remember the name.

Do you believe that violent video games make people more violent in real life? Many don’t believe so, but there is a sect of those who think there is a link between violent behavior and video games, especially when the game has carjackings, murder, and other criminal activities.

In 2021, GTA V was mentioned in law HB3531 filed in Illinois. The goal of this law was to prohibit the sale of games featuring “psychological harm.” Ultimately, it wanted to restrict the sale of games like GTA 5 that featured criminal activity, meaning GTA 5 would get banned.

This wasn’t the first time the series came under fire from lawmakers, and it probably won’t be the last, but it leaves a lasting impression that people still remember and will help GTA 5 live on.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hunger Games Suzanne Collins doesn't take a backseat to the movies, according to Sunrise on the Reaping director Francis Lawrence.
  • Before the latest novel was even published, it was confirmed a film adaptation would also be in the works, telling the prequel story of Haymitch Abernathy – the District 12 victor who went on to mentor Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hunger Games Suzanne Collins doesn't take a backseat to the movies, according to Sunrise on the Reaping director Francis Lawrence.

Before the latest novel was even published, it was confirmed a film adaptation would also be in the works, telling the prequel story of Haymitch Abernathy – the District 12 victor who went on to mentor Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

"Yeah, she's very involved," Lawrence tells us when we meet with him in London to discuss The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. "When she sends the manuscript, I read it, usually a couple times, and then the first thing we do is we sit in a conference room at the publishing company that she works through, and we break down the book together. And we've done that since Catching Fire.

"And then she's on the phone with me and Nina [Jacobson, producer] and the screenwriter every day for hours, probably hundreds of hours of calls talking through the script, and then she kind of disappears when we shoot," he continues. "And then we bring her back in when we have a cut, and she looks at the cut, and we give her the data on tests, and we decide if we have to do any pickups or anything. And then she obviously sees the finished product, so she is very, very involved. She's just not there on the shoot, and part of that is so that she can keep an objective perspective on it for when she sees the cut.".

While the Sunrise on the Reaping film has yet to be released to the public, it's already garnered strongly positive reactions from fans, which kicked off with an outpouring of love for each casting announcement.

Industry observers note that "It's wishy-washy with things online, and I feel like, in this day and age, it is a lot easier to be negative, and I feel like the negativity is always a little bit louder," says McKenna Grace, who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner. "And so, it's such a blessing whenever you're a part of a fan base, or whenever anything that you're a part of is getting positivity, and for it to be such an overwhelming, kind response, I feel like is just… But it's just been so wonderful that they're happy with it, and that they're accepting us into this franchise.".

In a recent development, joseph Zada, who plays Haymitch, adds: "And even a lot of the people that have been able to see it from press that haven't been fans, or haven't seen the previous films, are just also so excited to see it, which is such a scary thing. [You] walk into a prequel hoping that it can stand alone, and that people that aren't familiar with the franchise can enjoy the film, too.".

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters this November 20. In the meantime, check out our The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review and our guide to all the biggest movie release dates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Sources indicate that since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

It has been revealed that sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

After 13 long, long years of waiting, players are finally getting their hands on Grand Theft Auto 6. The opening hours spent exploring the Keys feel almost daunting, as the Herculean size and scope of Jason and Lucia's epic adventure become apparent. It's the type of game you want to pace yourself with, exploring every nook and cranny, appreciating every character, and seeing what Leonida has to offer.

There is, however, at the end of the first chapter, a pretty significant point of no return, and there are a couple of things you'll want to get in order before you progress. We won't tell you which story beats to hit, but we do have a couple of big recommendations for you before moving on.

Minor spoilers for Grand Theft Auto 6's Act 1 below.

Grand Theft Auto 6's first chapter finishes at the yacht party, when Lucia asks Jason if he's ready to take on Mattia's job. Upon accepting, the point of no return will be hit, and you will lose a lot. Any cash you have worked for will be gone, as will Jason's car, and certain stash points aren't safe.

In a recent development, there's no point spending too much money on Jason's car for this reason; it'll be gone after this point. The cash in your wallet and your stash will also disappear; you can save some in your Family Saver bank account, but anything in your standard bank will be lost. This means any big robberies or scores are not worth doing yet; save them for later in the game.

Recent findings suggest that while you lose your car, you won't lose your weapons or clothing. If you have excess cash, make sure to buy weapons, mods, and dress Jason up to the nines. At least your money won't go to waste then. Tattoos and his haircut also remain if you have a few extra bucks left after that.

It has been revealed that following this scene, you won't be returning to the Keys for a little while, so make sure to get all your affairs in order, and that you've done all the exploration you need to do. It seems disheartening, but the game really opens up from here, so don't sweat too much; it's just worth knowing that things take a bit of a turn after this point.
